definition: Data held out from training used to tune hyperparameters, select models, and detect overfitting — distinct from the final test set used only for evaluation.
details: Data held out from training used to tune hyperparameters, select models, and detect overfitting — distinct from the final test set used only for evaluation.

explainer.lead: Validation data is held out from training and used to tune hyperparameters, select models and detect overfitting. It matters because it keeps model-selection feedback separate from final evaluation.

tiers.eli5: It's the practice questions you use while studying, kept apart from the final exam.
tiers.practitioner: You tune hyperparameters and pick models against it, watching for overfitting. Pitfall: it is distinct from the final test set, which must be used only for evaluation.
tiers.paperLevel: Data held out from training, used for hyperparameter tuning, model selection and overfitting detection; separate from the test set used only for evaluation.

explainer.example: An engineer compares several models on the validation data to pick a configuration, then reports accuracy once on the untouched test set.
